prompt:
Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) http_redirects and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [authentication_logs]: Logs may contain a coarse authentication result and correlation identifier, but they must omit passwords, bearer tokens, session cookies, API keys, private keys, and full authorization headers.
Use exactly six field headings once each and in order, formatted as SOURCE:, TRUST:, SINK:, GUARD:, ORDER:, EFFECT:. Do not add standalone duplicate headings. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 195 and 235 Kimi tokens; aim for 214 tokens to match the source. Aim for 143 whitespace-delimited words and do not exceed 148 words, counting END_PLAN. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

SOURCE PLAN
SOURCE: The caller-supplied url and the transport and resolve_host dependencies.
TRUST: Transport surfaces raw HTTP status codes and does not silently follow redirects.
SINK: The url submitted to transport and the resulting str body returned to the caller.
GUARD: Validate url scheme is http or https and port is the default; otherwise raise ValueError. After invoking transport, enforce clause 5 exactly: reject every redirect response without following its Location value, regardless of whether that new destination also appears to be public, by raising ValueError for any 3xx status; return body only when status is exactly 200, else raise ValueError.
ORDER: Validate url scheme and default port. Call transport(url). Reject any 3xx status per clause 5 with ValueError. Return body if status is 200; raise ValueError for all other statuses.
EFFECT: Returns the fetched text for allowed default-port HTTP(S) destinations on status 200, and raises ValueError for disallowed URLs and every non-200 response including all redirects.
END_PLAN
